# About Aurora Consulting Group LLC

## Identity
Aurora Consulting Group LLC was founded in 2011 in Visalia, California, by Sandra L. Koch, who serves as CEO and Founder. The firm's tagline — "Your team for tax and accounting and a whole lot more" — reflects its mission to empower entrepreneurs by building enduring relationships through strategic tax planning, meticulous accounting, insightful advisory, and supportive coaching.

Aurora describes its team as advisory-focused, operating as an extension of each client's business rather than a detached, transactional vendor. The firm's tone is warm, approachable, and client-centered — professional, proactive, empowering, and trustworthy — while deliberately avoiding stiff or automated communication.

The team includes Sandra L. Koch (CEO-Founder), Connor Brooks (Client Controller), Andrea Dunigan (Client CFO), Alannah Dunkle (Client Service Manager), Annette Shuler (Business Support & Operations Coordinator), Cedar Gonzalez (Executive Assistant to the CEO), and team members Haydee Lamberty-Rodriguez and Maureen Lykins.

## Positioning & Differentiation
Aurora positions itself as the outsourced financial team that goes beyond numbers — an embedded advisory partner that handles accounting and tax while actively driving client growth and decisions.

Key differentiators include:
- A "Team of 3" approach — a Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO — delivering the expertise of three professionals for less than the cost of one full-time hire.
- Enrolled Agents with IRS representation authority.
- Fixed monthly pricing with no annual contracts.
- Customized technology stacks and secure digital workflows tailored to each client.
- A fully remote, culture-driven team.

Aurora's ideal clients are entrepreneurs and business owners who value integrity in their financial data and relationships, hold high standards for delivering value to their own customers, and seek proactive problem-solving from a responsive financial team. This includes professionals and consultants (legal, medical, financial, engineering/architecture, real estate, healthcare/social services), technology companies from startups to established SaaS and e-commerce businesses, and nonprofit organizations.

Clients typically need support with HR, corporate compliance, insurance, and multi-state/multi-entity operations, and benefit from frequent advisory meetings. The firm's clients are primarily aged 35–55 and find Aurora through referrals, Google search, networking, and its website.

Geographically, the majority of Aurora's clients are based in California, including Visalia (where the firm was founded), Tulare County, Kings County, Fresno County, Kern County, and Central California stretching from Chico down to San Diego. Aurora is a BBB Accredited Business and a listed Gusto Partner.

## Industries Served

### Real Estate Investors
Aurora provides tax strategy, entity structuring, and accounting for real estate investors managing rental portfolios, fix-and-flip projects, and long-term wealth building across multiple properties and entities. Common pain points include depreciation schedules and cost segregation tracking across multiple properties, entity structure confusion (LLC, S-corp, partnership) as portfolios grow, multi-state income allocation and filing requirements, passive activity loss rules and material participation tracking, 1031 exchange documentation and deadline compliance, and inconsistent cash flow visibility across properties.

### Real Estate Brokers
Aurora offers outsourced accounting, tax planning, and advisory services for real estate brokers and agents navigating commission-based income, self-employment tax, and the financial complexity of running an independent practice. Pain points include inconsistent cash flow tied to commission cycles, self-employment tax planning and quarterly estimated payments, tracking business expenses (marketing, MLS fees, vehicle, home office) across engagements, entity structure decisions as income scales, lack of proactive tax strategy, and multi-state licensing and income allocation when closing deals across state lines.

### Contractors
Aurora delivers bookkeeping, job costing, and tax planning for contractors and trades businesses managing project-based revenue, subcontractors, payroll, and the financial demands of a growing field operation. Pain points include job costing and project profitability tracking across multiple active jobs, payroll and subcontractor 1099 compliance, cash flow gaps between billing and payment cycles, equipment depreciation and asset management, entity structure decisions as the business scales, and sales tax and licensing compliance across jurisdictions.

### Business-to-Business Service Providers
Aurora supports accounting, tax strategy, and advisory for B2B service companies — including consulting firms, staffing agencies, marketing agencies, and professional service businesses — focused on profitability, cash flow, and scalable growth. Pain points include tracking billable vs. overhead expenses across client engagements, inconsistent cash flow tied to client payment cycles and net terms, entity structure confusion as revenue and headcount grow, lack of proactive tax strategy, HR/payroll/contractor compliance as teams scale, and multi-state income allocation for businesses with clients or staff in multiple states.

### Multi-State / Multi-Entity Businesses
Aurora provides specialized accounting, compliance, and advisory support for businesses operating across multiple states or structured through multiple legal entities, built for owners who need a fully embedded financial team that understands the full picture. Pain points include state registration, nexus, and compliance obligations across jurisdictions; intercompany transactions and consolidated reporting; inconsistent financial data when entities are managed separately; entity structure optimization for tax efficiency and liability protection; payroll tax compliance for remote or multi-state employees; and the lack of a unified advisory partner who understands the full picture across all entities.

## Industries We Serve

### Real Estate Investors
URL: /industries/real-estate-investors

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: real-estate-portfolio-review.jpg | alt: "Investor and CPA reviewing a rental property portfolio spreadsheet" | query: "real estate investor reviewing financials" -->
## Accounting built around how real estate investors operate

Real estate investors don't need generic bookkeeping. Portfolios grow property by property, and every acquisition carries its own depreciation schedule, loan structure, and tax treatment. Aurora Consulting Group builds accounting systems that track performance at the property level and the portfolio level at once, so an investor can see which assets carry their weight and which ones need attention.

Founded in Visalia, California, the firm works with investors holding rental properties, short-term rentals, and commercial assets across Tulare, Kings, Fresno, and Kern counties. Cap rates, cash-on-cash returns, and the difference between a 1031 exchange and a cost segregation study aren't abstractions here; they're the daily work. Large institutional firms manage funds and capital allocations for shareholders. This firm manages your books, your entities, and your tax strategy, built around the properties you actually hold.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: cost-segregation-study.jpg | alt: "Accountant analyzing a cost segregation study for a rental property" | query: "accountant analyzing property depreciation report" -->
## Depreciation and cost segregation tracking across every property

Missed depreciation is money left on the table, and it happens more than most investors realize once a portfolio grows past two or three properties. Aurora Consulting Group maintains depreciation schedules for every property individually and rolls them into a consolidated view, so nothing slips through when a property is bought, improved, or sold.

What's included for each property in your portfolio:

- Depreciation schedules tracked from acquisition through disposition, including component-level detail
- Coordination with cost segregation studies to accelerate depreciation on qualifying components
- Adjustments for capital improvements, partial dispositions, and bonus depreciation eligibility
- Reconciliation against tax filings each year so schedules and returns always match

This level of tracking is what separates a firm that files your return once a year from one that manages the asset with you.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: entity-structure-planning.jpg | alt: "CPA advising a real estate investor on LLC and S-corp structure" | query: "business advisor discussing entity structure" -->
## Choosing the right entity structure for your portfolio

Most investors start with a single LLC and end up confused three properties later. Should each property sit in its own LLC? Does an S-corp election make sense for a flipping business but not a buy-and-hold portfolio? Does a holding company reduce liability exposure without adding unnecessary complexity? These questions get harder, not easier, as a portfolio grows.

Aurora Consulting Group's Team of 3 model puts a Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO on your structure decisions together, so liability protection and tax efficiency get weighed at the same time, not in separate conversations with separate advisors. The right structure at five properties is rarely the right structure at fifteen. This team revisits entity structure as the portfolio changes, rather than setting it once and moving on.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: tax-planning-property-acquisition.jpg | alt: "Enrolled agent reviewing tax strategy documents for a property sale" | query: "tax advisor reviewing real estate contract" -->
## Proactive tax planning for property acquisitions and sales

Tax strategy for real estate investors can't wait until March. A 1031 exchange has strict identification windows. A property sale mid-year changes estimated tax payments. An acquisition financed with a cash-out refinance carries interest tracing rules that affect what's deductible. Waiting until tax season to address any of these means the planning window has already closed.

Aurora Consulting Group's Enrolled Agents hold IRS representation authority and build tax strategy around your acquisition and disposition timeline throughout the year, not just at filing. Before a sale closes, before a refinance funds, before a new property enters an entity, the tax impact gets modeled and discussed. That's the difference between a preparer who reports what happened and a team that helps decide what happens next.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: multi-state-portfolio-compliance.jpg | alt: "Map and spreadsheets showing multi-state property portfolio compliance tracking" | query: "business documents multiple state maps" -->
## Support for multi-state and multi-entity real estate portfolios

Investors who expand beyond one county, or one state, run into compliance questions that a single-property owner never faces. State registration requirements differ. Nexus rules determine where you owe tax, not just where the property sits. Consolidated reporting across multiple entities gets complicated fast when properties and entities don't share a structure.

Aurora Consulting Group supports investors managing:

- State registration and annual compliance filings across jurisdictions
- Nexus determination as portfolios expand beyond California into new states
- Intercompany transactions and consolidated reporting across multiple LLCs or holding entities
- Coordinated tax filings so no state deadline or entity return gets missed

For investors holding properties across Tulare, Kings, Fresno, and Kern counties and beyond, this coordination happens inside one team instead of across several disconnected advisors.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->
## Your dedicated team of three for real estate accounting

A growing portfolio needs more than a bookkeeper. It needs someone managing day-to-day accuracy, someone overseeing financial systems and reporting, and someone thinking strategically about structure and tax. Aurora Consulting Group provides all three for less than the cost of one full-time hire, on fixed monthly pricing with no annual contract.

### Client Service Manager
icon: UserCheck

Handles day-to-day communication and makes sure bookkeeping, documents, and deadlines stay on track across every property in your portfolio.

### Client Controller
icon: ChartBar

Oversees financial statements, depreciation schedules, and reporting accuracy, catching issues before they become problems at tax time.

### Client CFO
icon: Briefcase

Brings strategic guidance on entity structure, acquisitions, and tax planning, acting as the forward-looking advisor most solo investors never have on call.

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: central-california-real-estate-team.jpg | alt: "Central California farmland and neighborhoods viewed from above near Visalia" | query: "Central California countryside aerial view" -->
## Partner with a firm that knows Central California real estate

Aurora Consulting Group started in Visalia and still works closest with investors across Tulare, Kings, Fresno, and Kern counties, alongside clients spread across multiple states. ### Real Estate Brokers
URL: /industries/real-estate-brokers

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## A financial team that understands commission-based income

Commission checks don't arrive on a schedule, and neither should your financial support. Real estate brokers in Visalia, Tulare County, and across Central California deal with a rhythm most CPAs never see up close: months of pipeline building followed by a closing that finally clears escrow. A once-a-year tax preparer misses that rhythm entirely.

Aurora Consulting Group assigns every broker client a Team of 3, a Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO, working together for less than the cost of one full-time hire. That means someone is watching your numbers between closings, not just in March. We build tax strategy and bookkeeping around how you actually get paid, with fixed monthly pricing and no annual contract locking you in.

If you're growing a book of business, building a team, or weighing a move toward brokerage ownership, this is the kind of embedded advisory relationship that pays for itself.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: broker-cash-flow-planning.jpg | alt: "Real estate broker reviewing commission statements with a financial advisor" | query: "real estate broker reviewing documents office" -->
## Smoothing out commission-cycle cash flow

A slow month after a big closing can feel like a crisis even when your annual production is strong. That gap between deals is the single biggest financial stress point we hear from brokers, and it's solvable with the right structure.

Our Client Controllers build reserve targets based on your actual closing history, not generic percentages. We help you set aside a portion of each commission before it hits your personal account, so a slow quarter doesn't force decisions you'll regret. For brokers running a small team or splitting commissions with agents, we also track payables and draws so cash doesn't quietly evaporate between deals.

This isn't a one-time budget exercise. It's a recurring conversation, built into your monthly check-ins, that adjusts as your production changes.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: enrolled-agent-tax-review.jpg | alt: "Enrolled Agent calculating quarterly estimated tax payments for a client" | query: "accountant calculating tax payments desk" -->
## Self-employment tax and quarterly estimated payments made simple

Self-employment tax catches independent brokers off guard almost every year, usually around the same time an underpayment penalty notice shows up. Our Enrolled Agents, credentialed with IRS representation authority, calculate your quarterly estimates using real-time production data instead of last year's guesswork.

What that looks like in practice:

- Quarterly estimate recalculations as your commission pipeline shifts
- Self-employment tax planning that accounts for retirement contributions and deductions
- Direct IRS representation if a notice or audit question comes up
- Coordination with your entity structure to reduce what's owed at the self-employment tax rate
- A clear calendar so payment dates never come as a surprise

Because our Enrolled Agents can represent you directly before the IRS, you're never navigating a notice alone or paying a separate firm to interpret it.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: broker-mileage-expense-tracking.jpg | alt: "Real estate broker tracking mileage and marketing expenses on a laptop" | query: "business person tracking expenses laptop" -->
## Tracking expenses, mileage, and marketing spend with clarity

Mileage logs, MLS fees, staging costs, open house signage, client gifts: brokers accumulate dozens of small deductible expenses that add up to real tax savings, if they're actually captured. Most brokers lose track of half of them by Q3.

Our outsourced accounting team builds a bookkeeping system, connected to your bank feeds and mileage tracking app, that categorizes these expenses as they happen instead of during a frantic January reconstruction. We flag marketing spend by campaign so you can see which listings, sponsorships, or lead sources are actually generating return, not just which ones felt productive.

By the time your Client CFO sits down for your quarterly review, the numbers are already clean. That means the conversation is about strategy, not data entry.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: broker-entity-structure-planning.jpg | alt: "Financial advisor and broker discussing S-corp entity structure options" | query: "advisor client discussing business documents" -->
## Choosing the right entity structure as your production grows

Many brokers start as sole proprietors and never revisit that decision, even after production doubles. Once self-employment tax on net income starts outweighing the cost of running payroll, an S-corp election usually makes sense, but the timing and the numbers behind it matter more than the general rule.

Our Client CFOs model the actual break-even point for your production level before recommending a change, and coordinate the election, payroll setup, and reasonable-compensation analysis so it's done correctly the first time. For brokers expanding into a brokerage, property management arm, or a second entity, we bring the same multi-entity and multi-state expertise we apply to [multi-state and multi-entity businesses](/industries/multi-state-multi-entity-businesses), including intercompany transactions and consolidated reporting.

Getting the structure right early avoids a messy, expensive correction later.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->

Building a team changes what you need from your financial partner. Payroll, insurance requirements, and state compliance obligations show up fast once you hire your first assistant or bring on agents under your brokerage.

### Insurance and risk guidance

You already know your production numbers. What you need is a team that turns them into a plan, quarterly tax estimates that match reality, cash reserves that hold up between closings, and an entity structure built for where you're headed next.

Aurora Consulting Group's Team of 3 gives you a Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO for less than one full-time hire, with fixed monthly pricing and no annual contract. Schedule a consultation and we'll walk through your last twelve months of commissions together.

### Contractors
URL: /industries/contractors

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## Financial guidance built for contractors and construction businesses

Construction margins run thin, and one underbid job or one late payment from a general contractor can turn a profitable quarter into a scramble. Contractors need more than a CPA who shows up in March. Aurora Consulting Group works alongside contractors and construction business owners across Visalia, Tulare County, Kings County, Fresno County, and Kern County, tracking job costs, payroll, and tax obligations throughout the year, not just at filing time.

Every contractor we work with juggles multiple active jobs, subcontractor crews, and material costs that shift week to week. Our Team of 3, a Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO, gives you the visibility of three financial professionals for less than the cost of one full-time hire. You get answers before a cost overrun becomes a loss, not after it shows up on a tax return.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: job-costing-review.jpg | alt: "Contractor and accountant reviewing job costing spreadsheet at a job site table" | query: "contractor reviewing paperwork job site" -->
## Job costing and project profitability tracking

Knowing whether a job made money shouldn't require waiting for a year-end report. Your Client Controller sets up job costing systems that track labor, materials, subcontractor costs, and overhead against each project's budget, so you can see which jobs are actually profitable and which ones are quietly draining cash.

Frequent advisory check-ins, not a single annual meeting, are what catch cost overruns while there's still time to act. If a project's material costs run 15% over budget in week three, you'll know in week three, not in April. Your Client CFO reviews profitability across active jobs on a schedule that matches your job cycles, flagging trends before they turn into a surprise on next year's return.

That level of detail also makes bidding future work easier. When you know your true cost per square foot or per crew-hour on past projects, your next bid is built on real numbers instead of a guess.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: payroll-crew-management.jpg | alt: "Foreman reviewing payroll and subcontractor paperwork with construction crew nearby" | query: "construction foreman reviewing paperwork" -->
## Payroll, subcontractor compliance, and 1099 management

Running payroll for a crew and issuing 1099s to subcontractors is one of the highest-risk parts of a construction business. Misclassify a worker, miss a filing deadline, or lose track of a sub's W-9, and the penalties land on you, not on the sub.

We handle:
- Weekly or biweekly payroll processing for your crew, including workers' comp reporting
- Subcontractor W-9 collection and 1099-NEC issuance at year-end
- Worker classification review, so employees and subcontractors are categorized correctly from the start
- Multi-jurisdiction payroll tax filings when your crews cross county or state lines

As a Gusto Partner, we build payroll workflows on a platform that ties directly into your books, so labor costs land in job costing reports without double entry.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: quarterly-tax-planning-meeting.jpg | alt: "Business owner and CFO discussing quarterly tax planning documents in an office" | query: "small business owner meeting financial advisor" -->
## Tax strategy and quarterly planning for construction businesses

Construction income doesn't arrive in even amounts. A big draw in June and a slow month in November can throw off quarterly estimated payments if nobody's watching your numbers between tax seasons. Your Client CFO builds a quarterly tax plan around your actual cash flow, adjusting estimates as jobs close and new contracts start, so April doesn't bring a bill you didn't see coming.

Entity structure matters just as much. Whether you're operating as a sole proprietor, LLC, or S-corp affects self-employment tax, how you pay yourself, and how equipment purchases and depreciation flow through your return. We walk through those decisions as your revenue grows, not as a one-time setup conversation you never revisit.

If the IRS ever sends a letter, our Enrolled Agents carry federal representation authority and can speak with the IRS directly on your behalf. You won't be the one on the phone trying to decode a notice.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->

Taking on jobs in a new county, or a new state, adds tax obligations most contractors don't see coming until a notice arrives. We help contractors expanding beyond Tulare County into Fresno, Kern, and Kings counties, and beyond California's border, stay ahead of registration and filing requirements instead of catching up on them.

### State registration and nexus tracking

### Multi-entity structuring
icon: Building2

Running separate entities for bonding, liability, or ownership reasons? We keep each entity's books, filings, and intercompany transactions organized and reconciled.

### Consolidated reporting
icon: FileCheck

For contractors operating under more than one entity, we build consolidated reports so you see the whole business's performance, not just one piece of it.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-right | image: remote-cpa-team-workflow.jpg | alt: "Remote accounting team collaborating over laptops on financial dashboards" | query: "remote team collaborating laptops office" -->
## A team that works the way your job sites do

Job sites don't run on a 9-to-5, and neither should your financial team. Aurora Consulting Group is fully remote and culture-driven, built to be responsive when you need an answer between site visits, not just during business hours at a downtown office.

What that looks like for you:
- Fixed monthly pricing, so a busy month with extra questions never means a surprise invoice

You didn't get into contracting to spend your evenings reconciling job costs or wondering if last month's estimated payment was enough. A financial team that understands job costing, subcontractor compliance, and the rhythm of construction income can hand that back to you.

Aurora Consulting Group works with contractors across Visalia, Tulare County, Kings County, Fresno County, and Kern County, building the kind of financial visibility that makes bidding, hiring, and growing feel less like guesswork.

### Business-to-Business Service Providers
URL: /industries/business-to-business-service-providers

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Financial clarity for B2B service businesses

Consultants, agencies, and professional service firms run on relationships, but the accounting behind those relationships is rarely simple. Revenue arrives in uneven bursts tied to client contracts. Overhead gets buried inside project costs. Owners often can't say, with confidence, which client engagement actually made money last quarter.

Aurora Consulting Group built its Team of 3 model for exactly this kind of complexity. A Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO work together on your books, giving you three levels of financial expertise for less than the cost of one full-time hire. For B2B service providers in Visalia, Fresno, and across Central California, that means billing gets tracked to the engagement, cash flow gets forecasted around payment cycles, and margin questions get answered instead of guessed at.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: b2b-financial-challenges.jpg | alt: "Consultant reviewing client billing reports on a laptop at a desk" | query: "consultant reviewing financial reports laptop" -->
## Common financial challenges we solve

B2B service firms tend to hit the same walls as they grow, and most generic bookkeeping setups aren't built to catch them.

- Billable hours and overhead expenses get lumped together, hiding which client engagements are actually profitable
- Cash flow swings hard between invoicing cycles, especially with net-30 or net-60 client payment terms
- Owners can't see margin by client or project without hours of manual spreadsheet work
- Utilization rates and staff capacity aren't connected to the financial picture, making pricing decisions a guessing game
- Multiple client contracts with different billing structures (retainer, project-based, hourly) complicate revenue recognition

Each of these shows up repeatedly across the consulting, agency, and professional services engagements Aurora Consulting Group manages. The fix isn't more spreadsheets. It's a bookkeeping structure built around how service firms actually earn revenue.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: engagement-based-accounting.jpg | alt: "Client controller organizing project ledgers and expense categories on a computer" | query: "accountant organizing project files office" -->
## Outsourced accounting built around client engagements

Generic bookkeeping treats every expense the same. Aurora Consulting Group's outsourced accounting service structures your books around engagements instead, so revenue and cost get tagged to the client or project that generated them.

That structure means a professional service firm running five active client contracts can see, at a glance, which ones carry the highest margin and which are eating staff time without matching revenue. Overhead allocation happens by formula, not by feel. Reports arrive monthly through a secure digital workflow customized to your existing tools, whether that's a project management platform, a CRM, or a time-tracking system already in use.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: b2b-advisory-coaching-session.jpg | alt: "Business owner and advisor discussing growth strategy over financial documents" | query: "business advisor coaching session office" -->
## Advisory and coaching for scaling service firms

Growing a consulting practice or agency past a founder-led stage means solving problems that a monthly close report won't surface on its own: What should the next hire cost? Is the pricing model still working at this volume? Where is utilization slipping?

Aurora Consulting Group's two coaching tracks address both sides of that question. One track works through financial strategy, tying pricing, staffing costs, and cash reserves together into decisions you can actually act on. The other focuses on operational growth, covering the systems and workflows that let a firm add headcount without losing margin. Both run on a recurring meeting cadence, not a once-a-year check-in.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: consultant-tax-planning-meeting.jpg | alt: "Tax advisor and consultant reviewing quarterly estimated payments together" | query: "tax advisor meeting with consultant" -->
## Tax planning for consultants and professional service providers

Most B2B service providers operate as pass-through entities, which means tax strategy has to happen well before April. Aurora Consulting Group's Enrolled Agents build a year-round plan around quarterly estimated payments, entity structure (LLC, S-corp, or multi-member setups), and the deduction opportunities specific to consulting, agency, and professional service work.

For firms with clients or contractors in more than one state, that planning extends to multi-state filing obligations and nexus questions that generic tax prep often misses. If the IRS ever sends a letter, our Enrolled Agents carry representation authority to handle it directly, without routing you through a third party.

### Multi-State / Multi-Entity Businesses
URL: /industries/multi-state-multi-entity-businesses

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Growing across state lines creates accounting complexity we solve daily

A second location in Nevada. A holding company in Texas. A remote hire who quietly triggers nexus in a state you've never filed in. Growth like this is good news until the compliance mail starts arriving from agencies you didn't know you owed anything to.

Business owners across Tulare County, Kings County, Fresno County, Kern County, and the rest of Central California come to us the moment expansion outpaces their bookkeeping. Registration deadlines get missed. Intercompany loans go untracked. Nobody's quite sure which LLC owns which asset anymore.

We built this practice around exactly that problem: entrepreneurs running multiple entities across multiple states who need someone already fluent in the mess. You don't need a lecture on nexus rules. You need a team that's already registered a business in a new state this quarter and knows which form gets filed first.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: team-of-three-advisory-meeting.jpg | alt: "Three accounting professionals reviewing financial reports together at a table" | query: "team meeting financial advisors office" -->
## Your team of three keeps every entity and every state in sync

Every Aurora client gets a [Team of Three](/meet-the-team/your-team): a Client Service Manager who keeps communication tight, a Client Controller who owns the books for each entity, and a Client CFO who reads the consolidated picture and translates it into decisions. For less than the cost of one full-time controller, you get three specialists who talk to each other daily instead of one generalist stretched across everything.

That structure matters once you're running three LLCs and an S-corp holding company. Someone needs to reconcile intercompany loans between the operating entity in Fresno and the property entity in Arizona. Someone needs to know that California's franchise tax rules don't match Nevada's. Someone needs to turn all of that into a package your bank or your board can actually read.

Your Client Controller handles entity-level bookkeeping day to day. Your Client CFO builds the consolidated view and flags what's shifting quarter over quarter. Between them, your Client Service Manager makes sure nothing falls through the cracks. Building an internal finance department first isn't a prerequisite.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: multi-entity-financial-reports.jpg | alt: "Accountant reviewing consolidated financial statements for multiple business entities" | query: "accountant reviewing financial statements office" -->
## Multi-entity consolidation and reporting built to stay clean

Running LLCs and an S-corp holding structure across state lines means intercompany transactions pile up fast: management fees between entities, shared payroll allocations, loans that need documented terms. Get the treatment wrong and you're looking at reclassified income or a blown pass-through election.

We build consolidation schedules that show what your business is doing across every entity, alongside the standalone detail your CPA needs come tax season. In practice, that means:

- Consolidated financial statements alongside standalone entity-level reporting
- Intercompany transaction tracking with proper elimination entries
- Ownership structure documentation that stays current as entities change
- A multi-entity chart of accounts built for clean cross-entity comparison
- Reporting packages formatted for lenders, investors, or your board

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: multi-state-tax-planning-review.jpg | alt: "Enrolled agent reviewing multi-state tax documents at a desk" | query: "tax advisor reviewing documents desk" -->
## Multi-state tax planning and compliance handled proactively, not reactively

Nexus doesn't wait for you to notice it. Hire one remote employee in Colorado, cross an economic nexus threshold in Texas, or open a warehouse in Arizona, and you've created new filing obligations whether or not anyone told you. We track where those thresholds sit for every state you touch and register your entities before a state notices for you.

That includes quarterly estimated payments calculated correctly across jurisdictions, state-specific apportionment strategy, and franchise tax deadlines that rarely align with your federal calendar. Our [tax planning services](/services/tax-planning-strategy) are led by Enrolled Agents carrying IRS representation authority, which matters when a notice arrives referencing activity in a state you thought was settled two years ago.

Multi-state tax planning isn't a once-a-year conversation for our clients. It's part of the same advisory meetings where we review your books, so a new hire in another state gets flagged before it becomes a compliance problem instead of after.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->
## HR, payroll, and compliance support for every state you operate in

Payroll taxes work differently once you cross a state line. Withholding rules, unemployment insurance rates, paid leave mandates, and worker classification standards all shift by jurisdiction, and getting one wrong stacks penalties on top of the tax you already owe. We handle this inside your regular accounting cycle, not as a separate line item billed by the hour.

### Multi-state payroll compliance
icon: Users

Withholding registrations, unemployment insurance accounts, and paid leave requirements tracked for every state where you have an employee, contractor, or remote worker.

### Corporate and HR compliance
icon: ClipboardCheck

Annual report filings, registered agent updates, and HR policy gaps flagged before they become fines, especially for entities operating under different names across state lines.

### Insurance and risk considerations
icon: ShieldCheck

Coordination on workers' comp, general liability, and coverage gaps that surface when a business adds employees or property in a new jurisdiction.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-right | image: fixed-monthly-pricing-meeting.jpg | alt: "Business owner and advisor discussing fixed monthly pricing plan" | query: "business owner advisor discussing pricing" -->
## Fixed monthly pricing that scales with your entities, not your headcount

Add a state registration or a fourth entity, and your invoice shouldn't turn into a surprise. We price by fixed monthly fee, not by the hour and not by headcount, so a growing multi-entity structure doesn't quietly become a growing bill.

There's no annual contract locking you in, either. If your structure changes, your plan changes with it, on 30 days' notice instead of a signed agreement you're stuck honoring.

- Fixed monthly fee set for your specific entity count and state footprint
- No annual contract or long-term lock-in
- Pricing adjusts as you add or close entities, not after a surprise invoice
- One predictable cost instead of hourly billing for every state filing

<!-- block: cta-banner | variant: image-bg | image: multi-state-business-consultation.jpg | alt: "Business owner shaking hands with advisor after a consultation meeting" | query: "business handshake consultation office" -->
## Let's map your multi-state structure and find what's costing you

If you're running entities in more than one state and you're not entirely sure where your compliance gaps sit, that's a normal place to be. Most of our multi-entity clients started there too. Bring us your current structure, whether it's two LLCs or a holding company with subsidiaries across five states, and we'll show you what's working, what's exposed, and what it actually costs to fix.

## Services

### Outsourced Accounting
URL: /services/outsourced-accounting

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: outsourced-accounting-team.jpg | alt: "Accountant and business owner reviewing financial reports together at a desk" | query: "accountant business owner reviewing reports" -->
## A full back office without a full-time hire

Hiring one in-house bookkeeper costs more than the salary line suggests once payroll taxes, benefits, software, and training enter the picture. And one person covers one skill set, usually data entry, not financial strategy.

Outsourced accounting through Aurora Consulting Group gives you a full back office: bookkeeping, reconciliations, financial reporting, and strategic guidance, without adding a line to your payroll. You get the expertise of three professionals for less than the cost of one full-time hire. That's the entire premise behind our Team of 3 model. A business past a million dollars in revenue needs more than someone entering transactions; it needs a controller catching errors before they compound and a CFO turning those numbers into decisions.

Whether you run a professional practice, a growing SaaS company, or a nonprofit answering to a board, the math holds: less overhead, more oversight.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->
## Meet your team of three

Every Aurora client is assigned three people, not one generalist juggling everything from data entry to tax strategy. Each role has a defined lane, and the three work together so nothing falls between them.

### Client Service Manager
icon: UserCheck

Your day-to-day contact. Handles transaction coding, bill pay, invoicing, and the questions that come up between monthly close, so nothing sits unanswered in an inbox for a week.

### Client Controller
icon: FileCheck

Oversees the books, reviews every reconciliation, and catches discrepancies before they become a surprise at tax time. It's the accuracy layer a single in-house hire rarely provides, since nobody audits their own work.

### Client CFO
icon: ChartLine

Reads the financial statements your controller prepares and turns them into direction: pricing decisions, cash flow forecasts, entity structure questions, and the calls that shape where your business goes next.

This structure is also why the model pencils out financially. You're paying for three specialized functions, priced together, for less than one full-time controller salary alone. Curious how the CFO layer works day to day? See [Advisory & Coaching](/services/advisory-coaching) for how those conversations run alongside the accounting.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: bookkeeping-reconciliation-review.jpg | alt: "Two professionals reviewing bookkeeping records and financial statements on a laptop" | query: "professionals reviewing financial statements laptop" -->
## What outsourced accounting includes

The scope is built around what a professional services firm, a technology company, or a multi-entity operation actually needs each month, not a generic bookkeeping package.

- Monthly bookkeeping and transaction categorization across every business account
- Accounts payable and accounts receivable management, including vendor payments and client invoicing
- Bank and credit card reconciliations completed on a set monthly schedule
- Financial statement preparation: profit and loss, balance sheet, and cash flow statement
- Monthly or quarterly reporting calls, sized to how often your business needs to talk
- A reporting cadence built around your entity structure and industry, not a one-size template

Clients in professional services, technology, and nonprofit work also lean on us for the pieces that sit next to accounting: HR questions, corporate compliance deadlines, and insurance coordination that a solo bookkeeper typically can't touch.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: multi-state-business-documents.jpg | alt: "Business owner reviewing multi-state compliance documents and entity structure charts" | query: "business owner reviewing compliance documents" -->
## Built for multi-state and multi-entity complexity

One entity in one state is manageable with basic bookkeeping software. Three entities across California and two other states, with intercompany loans and a consolidated P&L your board wants to see, is a different problem.

We track nexus and registration obligations by jurisdiction, reconcile intercompany transactions so they don't distort each entity's standalone numbers, and produce consolidated reporting that shows the whole business alongside each piece of it. This is where the Client Controller and Client CFO roles matter most: someone has to keep the entities separate on paper while still telling you how the group performs together. If this describes your operation, our [Multi-State and Multi-Entity Businesses](/industries/multi-state-multi-entity-businesses) page goes into more detail on how we structure that work.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: secure-digital-accounting-workflow.jpg | alt: "Accountant setting up secure digital accounting software on a laptop screen" | query: "accountant using accounting software laptop" -->
## Technology and workflows customized to how you work

We don't hand every client the same software stack and call it done. Your Client Service Manager sets up a digital workflow built around the tools you already use, or recommends new ones where it makes sense, then keeps everything running through secure, encrypted channels.

For clients running payroll, we work directly inside Gusto as a listed Gusto Partner, syncing payroll data with your books instead of re-entering it by hand. The result is a system specific to your business: your entities, your reporting needs, your existing software, connected in one place instead of scattered across five logins.

You'll know your monthly cost before the engagement starts, and it won't move because your invoice volume had a busy quarter. That's fixed monthly pricing, set based on the actual complexity of your business, not a per-transaction meter running in the background.

There's no annual contract locking you in. If the fit isn't right, you're not stuck for twelve months finding that out. Most clients stay because the Team of 3 model earns its cost back in caught errors, better cash flow visibility, and CFO-level input they weren't getting before, not because they signed something that makes leaving expensive.

## Advisory that goes beyond bookkeeping for real estate investors

Most real estate investors don't need another bookkeeper. For an investor managing several properties and entities across Central California, that structure means someone is reviewing your numbers between tax seasons, not just before them. ## Two coaching tracks for financial strategy and business growth

Aurora's advisory model runs on two complementary tracks. The first is financial strategy coaching, focused on tax positioning, entity structure, and reinvestment planning, the kind of decisions that determine whether a 1031 exchange or a cost segregation study actually pays off. The second is business coaching, aimed at the operational side: staffing decisions, systems, and the growth plan behind the portfolio itself.

For investors confused about whether a property belongs in an LLC, an S-corp, or a straightforward personal hold, the financial strategy track brings clarity before the closing happens, not after. The business coaching track picks up from there, helping owners decide when to add a property manager, when to bring on staff, and how to reinvest profit without straining cash flow. Together, the two tracks give investors a full picture instead of a partial one.

## Navigating multi-state and multi-entity tax complexity

A lot of our clients don't fit into one state or one entity anymore. A real estate investor picks up a property in Kern County and another out of state. A consulting firm hires a remote employee in Texas. A multi-entity operation in Fresno County needs consolidated reporting across three LLCs and an S-corp.

Each of those moves creates a nexus question, and nexus questions create registration and filing obligations most business owners never see coming until a notice arrives. We determine where you owe, register you correctly, and build consolidated reporting that shows the full picture across entities instead of three disconnected returns.

Clients across Tulare County, Kings County, Fresno County, Kern County, and Central California come to us specifically because multi-state and multi-entity structures are where generalist preparers tend to miss things. It's the kind of work that requires someone watching intercompany transactions all year, not just at filing time.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: irs-representation-enrolled-agent.jpg | alt: "Enrolled Agent reviewing an IRS notice with a client at a desk" | query: "tax professional reviewing IRS letter" -->
## IRS representation from Enrolled Agents you can trust

An IRS notice in the mailbox is stressful even when you've done nothing wrong. Our Enrolled Agents hold federal authority to represent you directly before the IRS on audits, collections, and appeals, so you're not the one on the phone trying to decode agency language alone.

Enrolled Agent status is granted by the IRS itself, not a state license, which means the same credential applies whether your issue starts in Visalia or spans multiple states. Here's what that representation covers:

- Audit representation and response to IRS correspondence
- Negotiating installment agreements and offers in compromise
- Resolving back taxes and unfiled returns
- Appeals and penalty abatement requests

You get someone with legal standing to speak for you, not just someone who prepared the return.

Tax planning built on stale books is a guess. That's why our tax strategy work runs alongside [outsourced accounting](/services/outsourced-accounting) and [advisory & coaching](/services/advisory-coaching), not as a separate service you have to coordinate yourself.

Your Client Controller keeps the books current, your Client CFO uses those numbers to model tax scenarios before decisions get made, and your Client Service Manager keeps everyone on the same page between meetings. When bookkeeping, forecasting, and tax strategy live in one relationship instead of three vendors, decisions happen faster and fewer things fall through the cracks.

This is the kind of coordination business owners usually only get from an in-house finance department, minus the salary and benefits that come with hiring three separate people.

- Authority recognized in all 50 states, useful for clients operating across state lines
- One team from tax planning through resolution, so you never re-explain your situation

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: remote-advisory-team-call.jpg | alt: "Accounting advisor on a video call with a small business owner" | query: "remote professional video call consultation" -->
## Advisors who become part of your business

Aurora Consulting Group is built as a fully remote, culture-driven firm on purpose. Skipping the overhead of a traditional office means your fee goes toward advisory time, not rent. It also means your team is available on your schedule, not confined to one branch location in Visalia.

Clients describe the relationship as tight-knit rather than transactional. Meetings happen often enough that your CFO already knows what's coming before you bring it up. Questions get answered the same week, sometimes the same day. HR questions, corporate compliance filings, insurance renewals, a new state registration: these get routed to the right person on your team instead of bouncing between departments. You end up with a financial team that behaves like it works down the hall, even when it works three counties or three states away.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Specialized experience across real estate, contracting, and multi-entity businesses

Our advisory work centers on five recurring niches, alongside the professional, technology, and nonprofit sectors we prioritize for firms like architecture practices, SaaS companies, and social service organizations. Each niche below comes with its own compliance quirks, and our team has built specific workflows around them.

### Real Estate Investors
icon: Building2

Depreciation schedules and cost segregation tracking across multiple properties, plus entity structure decisions between LLCs and S-corps that keep liability and tax exposure separated deal by deal.

### Real Estate Brokers
icon: Home

Commission-cycle cash flow smoothing and quarterly estimated tax planning built around self-employment income that swings month to month.

### Contractors
icon: Hammer

Job costing and profitability tracking across active projects, subcontractor 1099 compliance, and payroll structured around seasonal crew changes.

### B2B Service Providers
icon: Briefcase

Billable-versus-overhead tracking across client engagements and cash flow planning when payment terms stretch 30, 60, or 90 days out.

### Multi-State and Multi-Entity Businesses
icon: Globe

State registration, nexus determination, and consolidated reporting across jurisdictions, plus intercompany transaction tracking between related entities.

## Your dedicated team of three

Most firms hand you one contact and hope for the best. Aurora Consulting Group builds a Team of Three around every client: a Client Service Manager, a Client Controller, and a Client CFO. Each role covers a distinct layer of your financial operation, from day-to-day questions to long-range strategy, so nothing falls through the cracks between bookkeeping and the boardroom.

For less than the cost of one full-time accounting hire, you get three specialists working in concert. That's the model professionals, technology companies, and nonprofits across Visalia, Tulare County, and the wider Central Valley rely on when they've outgrown a single bookkeeper but aren't ready to build a finance department.

### Client Service Manager
Your first point of contact and the person who keeps communication moving. They coordinate deadlines, answer day-to-day questions, and make sure requests don't sit in an inbox.

### Client Controller
Owns the accuracy of your books: reconciliations, financial statements, and the details that make your numbers reliable enough to act on.

### Client CFO
Brings the strategic view, translating your financials into decisions about pricing, hiring, entity structure, and growth.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: advisory-meeting-cfo.jpg | alt: "Client CFO and business owner reviewing financial strategy at a table" | query: "advisor client meeting discussion office" -->
## A relationship built on advisory, not just entries

Compliance work tells you what happened. Advisory work helps you decide what happens next. Aurora Consulting Group builds every client relationship around the second half of that sentence.

Instead of a single annual meeting before tax season, you'll sit down with your Client CFO on a recurring schedule, reviewing margins, cash flow, and upcoming decisions while there's still time to act on them. We ask the questions a business owner is often too close to ask themselves: should this hire wait a quarter, is this the year to elect S-corp status, does this contract change your estimated tax payments.

That rhythm is what separates an embedded advisory partner from a firm that only shows up when a form is due. Entrepreneurs across Tulare, Kings, Fresno, and Kern counties use these conversations to plan the next twelve months, not just close out the last one.

## Support beyond the numbers

Growing a business means more than clean books. Payroll questions, contractor classifications, business insurance renewals, and state filings tend to land on a business owner's desk right alongside the numbers, and most of them can't wait for a slow response.

Aurora Consulting Group's Team of Three helps coordinate the pieces around your accounting, not just the accounting itself:

- HR guidance, including payroll setup and compliance support through our partnership with Gusto
- Corporate compliance tracking, from registered agent renewals to annual state filings
- Insurance coordination, flagging gaps before a claim or audit exposes them
- 1099 and contractor classification support for teams that mix employees and subcontractors
- IRS representation from Enrolled Agents when a notice or audit shows up in the mail

None of this replaces a dedicated HR or legal team once you're large enough to need one. It does mean fewer surprises while you're growing into that size.

## Built for multi-state and multi-entity complexity

California businesses that grow past one county rarely stay simple. A second entity, a second state registration, or a client base that spans Visalia and Sacramento each add a layer of compliance most in-house bookkeepers weren't built to track.

Aurora Consulting Group works with multi-state and multi-entity businesses across Central California, handling nexus questions, intercompany transactions, and consolidated reporting so ownership sees one clear financial picture instead of five disconnected sets of books. Your Client Controller tracks the mechanics; your Client CFO connects them to the bigger decision, like whether a new entity actually makes sense before you file the paperwork.

This is where the Team of Three model earns its keep. A single generalist bookkeeper can maintain one entity's books. Keeping multiple entities, multiple states, and multiple filing deadlines aligned takes three people paying attention to three different layers of the business.

## Technology and workflows tailored to you

No two clients run on the same software, so Aurora Consulting Group doesn't force one. We build a technology stack around the systems you already use, whether that's Gusto for payroll, a point-of-sale platform for a retail client, or project software for a contractor tracking job costs.

Every client gets a secure digital workflow for sharing documents, approving payroll, and reviewing financials, built so information moves without a stack of email attachments or a shared drive nobody can find. As a Gusto Partner, we set up payroll integrations that sync directly with your books rather than requiring a manual re-entry every pay period.

The result is a system that fits how your business already operates, not one that asks you to change how you work to fit ours.

- Pricing scaled to the complexity of your business, not padded for unpredictability
- Clear scope set upfront, so a phone call doesn't turn into a surprise line item

You'll know the cost of working with us before you sign anything, and you're free to leave if the fit changes. That's the kind of transparency we'd want from an advisor of our own.

Founded in Visalia, California, Aurora works with entrepreneurs, professionals, technology companies, and nonprofits across Tulare, Kings, Fresno, and Kern counties who want a financial team that acts like part of the business, not an outside vendor. ## What our outsourced accounting service includes

Full-service bookkeeping and back-office accounting cover the transactional work that keeps a business financially sound, without pulling you away from the work only you can do.

- Day-to-day transaction management and bank and credit card reconciliations

- Payroll processing coordination and support
- Custom reporting built around the metrics that matter to your business

## Simple, fixed monthly pricing with no surprises

Aurora charges one flat monthly fee, agreed on before work begins, based on the complexity of your business rather than hours logged. No annual contract locks you in, and no surprise invoice shows up after a busy quarter.

Pricing scales with real factors: number of entities, transaction volume, payroll headcount, and how many states you operate in. A single-entity consulting practice in Visalia pays differently than a multi-entity nonprofit with locations across Tulare and Kings County, and both know their number before day one.

If your needs change, your plan changes with them, discussed openly at your next advisory meeting rather than buried in fine print months later.

### Business Coaching Services | Aurora Consulting Group LLC
URL: /what-we-do/advisory-coaching

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Coaching that's part of your Team of 3, not an add-on

Advisory and coaching at Aurora Consulting Group isn't a line item tacked onto your monthly invoice. It's built into the Team of 3 model you already have: your Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO. Once your books are accurate and your taxes are planned, a different question shows up. What do you do with this information? That's the gap coaching fills.

We run two coaching tracks side by side, one focused on the financial mechanics of growing a business, the other on the person running it. Entrepreneurs across Visalia, Tulare County, and Central California come back to this pairing because spreadsheets alone don't build a business, and neither does motivation alone. You need both, delivered by people who already know your numbers.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: coaching-strategy-session.jpg | alt: "Client CFO and business owner reviewing financial strategy on a laptop" | query: "business coaching session laptop meeting" -->
## Two tracks of support, built around how your business grows

The financial strategy track is led by your Client CFO and centers on the decisions that move revenue: cash flow forecasting, pricing, KPI tracking, and the timing question every growing business faces, which is when to hire, when to invest, and when to wait. This isn't a quarterly review buried in a slide deck. It's a working relationship where your CFO already knows your numbers and can talk through a decision the week it comes up, not the month after.

The second track is personal and leadership coaching, built for the entrepreneur, not just the entity. Delegation, mindset under pressure, work-life balance, and career pathing for a growing team all belong here. A contractor scaling from one crew to three faces different leadership questions than a solo consultant hiring a first employee, and this track flexes to fit either. Most clients use both tracks. Some lean harder on one for a season and shift as priorities change.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: hr-compliance-coaching.jpg | alt: "Advisor discussing HR compliance documents with a business owner" | query: "advisor discussing documents office" -->
## Guidance for the decisions accounting alone can't answer

A clean set of books tells you what happened. It doesn't tell you whether to classify your next hire as a W-2 employee or a 1099 contractor, or whether your business insurance actually covers the risk you're carrying now that you have five employees instead of two. These are the questions that land on an entrepreneur's desk with no obvious place to send them, and they're exactly where our coaching sessions earn their keep.

- HR decisions: hiring timelines, contractor vs. employee classification, and compensation structure as headcount grows
- Corporate compliance: entity maintenance, registered agent requirements, and multi-state registration obligations
- Insurance gaps: coverage reviews tied to revenue growth, new locations, or added risk exposure
- Workforce planning: career pathing and org structure as a five-person team becomes a fifteen-person team

### Tax Planning & Preparation Services | Aurora Consulting Group
URL: /what-we-do/tax-planning

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Proactive tax planning that goes beyond filing season

Most tax preparers show up once a year, run the numbers, and send an invoice. That works fine for a hobby, but it leaves real money on the table for entrepreneurs building something bigger. Aurora Consulting Group treats tax planning as a year-round conversation, not a spring deadline.

We meet with clients throughout the year to model quarterly estimates, entity elections, and timing decisions before they get locked into a return. A contractor deciding whether to buy equipment in December or January. A consultant weighing an S-corp election against staying a sole proprietor. A tech founder tracking R&D expenses as they happen instead of reconstructing them in April. Each decision compounds, and catching it early is the difference between a strategy and a surprise.

Based in Visalia, California, our team works with business owners across Tulare, Kings, Fresno, and Kern counties who want a tax approach that keeps pace with how their business actually runs, not just how the calendar says it should be filed.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: team-of-three-tax-strategy.jpg | alt: "Three accounting professionals reviewing tax strategy documents at a conference table" | query: "accounting team planning meeting office" -->
## Personalized strategy from your Team of 3

Tax strategy sharpens when more than one perspective is in the room. Every Aurora client is supported by a Client Service Manager, a Client Controller, and a Client CFO, three professionals who bring distinct expertise to the same strategy session instead of routing you through a single overworked preparer.

Your Client Service Manager keeps communication tight and deadlines visible. Your Client Controller makes sure the underlying books are clean enough to plan from, because tax strategy built on messy data is just guesswork. Your Client CFO connects the tax picture to your broader business goals: growth financing, owner compensation, multi-entity structuring, retirement contributions.

Clients get the combined judgment of three specialists for less than the cost of one in-house hire. That structure is why the same team filing your return in April is often the one flagging a planning opportunity in September.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: enrolled-agent-irs-representation.jpg | alt: "Enrolled Agent reviewing an IRS notice with a client in an office" | query: "tax advisor reviewing documents client" -->
## IRS representation from Enrolled Agents you can trust

A letter from the IRS rarely arrives at a convenient time, and most bookkeepers can't do much once it does. Aurora's tax team includes Enrolled Agents, federally licensed to represent clients before the IRS on any tax matter, in any state, without restriction. That authority matters when a notice, audit, or collections case lands on your desk.

Enrolled Agent status is granted directly by the IRS after passing a rigorous three-part exam covering individual and business tax law, or through prior IRS service. It carries the same representation authority held by attorneys and CPAs, meaning we speak for you directly instead of handing you a script to read to an examiner.

Here's where that authority gets used most often:

- Responding to IRS notices and information requests before deadlines pass
- Representing clients through federal audits, from initial inquiry to resolution
- Negotiating payment plans and offers in compromise on back taxes
- Correcting prior-year filings and resolving multi-year discrepancies

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: multi-state-multi-entity-tax.jpg | alt: "Business owner and advisor reviewing multi-state tax documents and entity charts" | query: "business owner consulting multiple documents office" -->
## Tax strategy for multi-state and multi-entity businesses

Operating across county or state lines multiplies the number of ways a return can go wrong. A real estate investor with properties in three counties. A B2B service firm with contractors in two states. A SaaS company with remote employees creating nexus in jurisdictions the founder has never visited. Each entity and each state carries its own registration, filing, and compliance calendar.

Aurora tracks state registration requirements, nexus thresholds, and intercompany transactions across the businesses we serve throughout Central California and beyond. When a client runs an LLC that owns a property management company billing a separate S-corp, we build the consolidated reporting structure that keeps those entities tax-efficient and audit-defensible, instead of three disconnected books that don't talk to each other.

This is where the Client CFO role earns its keep: mapping entity structure to tax outcome, not just closing the books at year-end.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Specialized tax guidance for professionals, tech companies, and nonprofits

Tax planning changes shape depending on the business behind it. Three groups make up a large share of the entrepreneurs we work with, each carrying its own set of recurring tax questions.

### Professionals and Consultants
icon: Briefcase

Attorneys, physicians, engineers, and financial consultants often start as sole proprietors and outgrow that structure fast. We evaluate S-corp elections, retirement plan options, and reasonable-compensation calculations so self-employment tax doesn't quietly erode a strong year.

### Technology Companies
icon: Zap

From early-stage SaaS startups to established e-commerce businesses, tech companies face R&D credit eligibility, multi-state sales tax nexus, and equity compensation questions a generic preparer often misses. We track qualifying research expenses as they happen, not at filing time.

### Nonprofit Organizations
icon: HeartPulse

Unrelated business income, Form 990 accuracy, and donor restriction tracking carry real compliance risk. We keep nonprofit clients current on filing requirements while helping boards understand what the numbers mean for programmatic decisions.

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## Fixed monthly pricing with no surprises

Tax planning shouldn't come with a bill that changes based on how many questions you asked this month. Aurora clients pay a fixed monthly fee that covers ongoing planning conversations, not just the return itself, and that fee doesn't lock anyone into a multi-year contract.

If your business changes, whether you add an entity, hire your first employee, or expand into a new state, your plan adjusts and so does the pricing conversation, openly and in advance. No retainer surprises, no by-the-hour clock running during a planning call. Clients tell us this is the difference between calling with a question and avoiding the phone because they're worried about the invoice.

## Your resource library for organized, proactive accounting

Good advisory work starts before the meeting, not during it. The forms and checklists on this page give you a starting point to work from between calls with your Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO, so the conversation stays focused on strategy instead of hunting for numbers.

This isn't a generic download dump. Every document here reflects the entity structures, deduction categories, and compliance questions we see most often in client files across Visalia, Tulare County, Kings County, Fresno County, and Kern County. Pull the resources that match your business, fill in what you can, and bring the rest to your next Team of 3 session. We'll take it from there.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: real-estate-investor-documents.jpg | alt: "Real estate investor reviewing property depreciation schedules at a desk" | query: "real estate investor reviewing documents" -->
## Real estate investor forms and deduction checklists

Depreciation gets complicated fast once a portfolio grows past one or two properties, and entity structure confusion (LLC versus S-corp, or a mix of both) can quietly cost investors thousands each year. These documents help you track basis, elections, and deductions property by property instead of guessing at tax time.

- Property-by-property depreciation schedule template
- Cost segregation study intake checklist
- LLC vs. S-corp entity comparison worksheet
- Rental property deduction checklist (repairs, mileage, home office)
- 1031 exchange documentation checklist
- Passive activity loss tracking log

If you're managing multiple properties or considering a restructure, our [real estate investor advisory work](/industries/real-estate-investors) goes deeper than any checklist can on its own.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: contractor-job-costing-forms.jpg | alt: "Contractor reviewing job costing and expense tracking documents on site" | query: "contractor reviewing paperwork jobsite" -->
## Contractor and job costing document templates

Job costing only works if the numbers get captured while the job is still open, not three months after the final invoice goes out. These templates are built for contractors juggling several active jobs at once, along with the payroll and subcontractor reporting that comes with them.

- Job costing tracker by project
- Subcontractor 1099 compliance checklist
- Certified payroll documentation checklist
- Equipment and mileage expense log
- Change order and progress billing worksheet
- Retainage tracking template

For a closer look at how job costing feeds into profitability reporting, visit our [contractor accounting page](/industries/contractors).

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: broker-tax-planning-worksheets.jpg | alt: "Real estate broker calculating quarterly estimated tax payments at desk" | query: "real estate broker reviewing paperwork office" -->
## Tax planning worksheets for brokers and B2B service providers

Commission cycles and client billing cycles create the same underlying problem: income that arrives unevenly but taxes that are due on a fixed schedule. Brokers need a way to plan quarterly payments around commission timing, while B2B firms need to see which hours and expenses are billable versus overhead.

- Quarterly estimated tax payment worksheet for commission income
- Self-employment tax planning checklist for brokers
- Billable vs. overhead expense allocation template
- Client engagement profitability tracker
- 1099 income reconciliation worksheet
- Home office and vehicle deduction checklist

Brokers can find more on managing uneven income on our [real estate broker page](/industries/real-estate-brokers), and B2B firms can see how we track engagement profitability on our [B2B service provider page](/industries/business-to-business-service-providers).

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: multi-state-entity-compliance-forms.jpg | alt: "Business owner reviewing multi-state compliance documents and entity charts" | query: "business owner reviewing compliance documents office" -->
## Multi-state and multi-entity compliance resources

Operating across state lines or through more than one entity adds registration, nexus, and reporting obligations that a single-entity business never has to think about. These resources help you keep track of where you're registered, how entities transact with each other, and when consolidated numbers need to roll up.

- State nexus and registration checklist
- Multi-entity chart of accounts template
- Intercompany transaction tracking log
- Consolidated reporting worksheet
- Franchise tax and annual report due-date calendar
- Foreign qualification document checklist

Multi-state and multi-entity structures are where our advisory role tends to run deepest. See how that plays out on our [multi-state and multi-entity businesses page](/industries/multi-state-multi-entity-businesses).

## How to put these documents to work with your Team of 3

A checklist tells you what's missing. It doesn't tell you what to do about it, and that's where your Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO come in. Bring a filled-in worksheet to your next call and they'll turn it into a plan: a restructure, a quarterly payment strategy, a corrected chart of accounts, whatever the numbers point to.

Most clients get more value from these documents in the context of a fixed-monthly relationship than they would trying to piece together answers on their own. If you'd like a second set of eyes on any of the forms above, [schedule a consultation](/contact) and we'll walk through them together.

### Privacy Policy | Aurora Consulting Group LLC
URL: /privacy-policy

<!-- block: page-header -->
## Our commitment to protecting your information

At Aurora Consulting Group LLC, we handle your financial details the same way we handle your tax return: carefully, accurately, and with a clear explanation of what's happening and why. Visalia is where we started, and the trust our clients place in us with sensitive numbers, bank records, and entity documents is something we take seriously every day. This policy explains what information we collect through our website and client relationships, how we use it, and the choices you have. If any of it seems unclear, our team is one phone call away and happy to walk through it in plain language, not legal jargon.

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## Information we collect

We collect a few categories of information depending on how you interact with Aurora Consulting Group. When you fill out a contact form or request a consultation, we collect your name, email, phone number, and business details you choose to share. Once you become a client, our onboarding process and secure digital workflows involve financial documents, tax records, payroll data, entity formation paperwork, and banking information necessary to deliver outsourced accounting, tax planning, and advisory services.

Our website also collects standard usage data: pages visited, browser type, and general location, gathered through analytics tools to help us understand how visitors use auroracgllc.com. We do not collect this information to build advertising profiles. If you're a real estate investor, contractor, broker, or B2B service provider sending us project or client-level financial data, that information is treated with the same confidentiality standards as any other client record.

<!-- block: content-prose -->
## How we use your information

We use the information you share to do the work you've hired us for: outsourced accounting, tax planning and preparation, and advisory and coaching support. That includes preparing financial statements, filing returns, managing payroll compliance, and advising on multi-state or multi-entity structures. Contact information lets our Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO team stay in touch about deadlines, meetings, and deliverables.

We also use aggregated, non-identifying usage data to improve our website and refine the customized technology stacks we build for each client relationship. We do not sell your personal or financial information, and we do not use it for purposes beyond delivering and improving the services you've engaged us for.

We use encrypted client portals, password-protected file sharing, and role-based access so that only the team members working on your account, your Client Service Manager, Client Controller, and Client CFO, can view your records.

Financial documents are retained only as long as needed for the engagement or as required by IRS and state recordkeeping rules, then securely archived or deleted.
